articles.title: AI Pullback Raises the Cost of Data Center Financing
articles.summary: The recent pullback in AI stocks is spilling into credit markets, making some data center financing more expensive even as demand for computing power remains strong. MUFG Americas CFO Mark Thumser says lenders are becoming more selective and investors are demanding wider spreads and better terms. He also argues the massive AI infrastructure buildout remains a long-term, transformational trend. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss financing demand following Anthropic’s IPO, the outlook for global credit markets, and growing public resistance to data center development. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: The Bull Case for Britain
articles.summary: When it comes to the UK economy, the prevailing mood has been decidedly downbeat. But Morgan Stanley’s Chief UK Economist, Bruna Skarica, sees reasons to be more optimistic — from improving productivity and the potential benefits of AI adoption to signs of resilience among UK households and businesses. In this episode, Skarica joins host Merryn Somerset Webb to make the case for a more constructive outlook. They discuss the UK’s fiscal risks, what’s driving the recent improvement in productivity, whether AI could ultimately translate into higher wages and living standards and what a stronger economy could mean for UK markets over the next five years. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Anthropic’s IPO was great for the tech elite – and not so great for the rest of us | Steven Greenhouse
articles.summary: The company’s co-founders are now wildly rich, while countless Americans face AI-driven threats to their jobs and fears of a stock bubbleThe sultans of Silicon Valley and the wizards of Wall Street rejoiced this week when Anthropic raised an eye-popping $81bn in the largest initial public offering in history. They saw the AI company’s IPO as a gung-ho affirmation of Silicon Valley’s and Wall Street’s marriage of technology and capitalism.For many employees at the company that developed Claude, the public offering must have been a thing of dreams. With the IPO valuing Anthropic at $1.5tn, the company’s seven co-founders each came away with stakes worth about $20bn, while, by one estimate, 600 of Anthropic’s more than 5,000 employees will have holdings topping $100m and 2,800 others will have shares worth more than $10m.
